cues.zh: 如果我们只对这个流行病猛开药，是解决不了问题的。至少到目前为止还没有。

cues.en: How much do you think antidepressant use has gone up over the past
cues.zh: 你觉得过去

cues.en: twenty years?
cues.zh: 二十年里抗抑郁药的使用增长了多少？

cues.en: I'm I'm... Would you care to guess?
cues.zh: 我……我……你愿意猜一下吗？

cues.en: I like that guess. Seventeen hundred percent. It's gone up over over three hundred percent. So you're close.
cues.zh: 我喜欢这个猜测。1700%。它上涨了超过300%。所以你猜得接近。

cues.en: Over three hundred percent.
And what's happened to the rate of depression
cues.zh: 那这段时间里抑郁症的发病率

cues.en: in the interim?
cues.zh: 发生了什么变化？

cues.en: It's continued to increase.
cues.zh: 它还在持续上升。

cues.en: One in nine Americans over the age of 12 is currently taking an antidepressant.
cues.zh: 目前每九个12岁以上的美国人中，就有一人在服用抗抑郁药。

cues.en: One in nine.
cues.zh: 九分之一。

cues.en: Currently, one in five, according to some estimates, have tried it at some point.
cues.zh: 目前，据一些估计，五分之一的人曾在某个时候尝试过它。

cues.en: Have we solved the epidemic? No. We haven't made a dent.
cues.zh: 我们解决这场流行病了吗？没有。我们几乎毫无进展。

cues.en: The answer, I believe, is a change of lifestyle. Now,
cues.zh: 我相信，答案是改变生活方式。现在，

cues.en: you'll see behind you a list of six lifestyle elements. When my research team and I, seven years ago, had this epiphany.
cues.zh: 你身后会显示一份包含六个生活方式要素的清单。七年前，我和研究团队灵光一现。

cues.en: We got together and we started scouring through the depressive literature,
cues.zh: 我们聚在一起，开始翻遍抑郁症相关文献，

cues.en: asking the question, what are the Kahluly doing that's protecting them? Specifically, based on everything we know about depression.
cues.zh: 问一个问题：Kahluly 人做了什么让他们受到保护？具体来说，是基于我们对抑郁症的全部了解。

cues.en: What did our ancestors do that protected them? And we quickly found six factors
cues.zh: 我们的祖先做了什么来保护自己？我们很快找到了六个因素

cues.en: that changed neurochemistry.
cues.zh: 这些因素改变了神经化学。

cues.en: Six factors that are known to be antidepressant.
cues.zh: 这六个因素已知具有抗抑郁作用。

cues.en: Six factors that we can reclaim and weave into the fabric of our day to day life in the present to protect ourselves from this devastating illness. And so we designed a new treatment program. It was really ambitious.
cues.zh: 我们可以重新拾回这六个因素，把它们织入当下的日常生活，从而保护自己免受这种毁灭性疾病侵害。于是我们设计了一个新的治疗方案。它确实雄心勃勃。

cues.en: I admit that.
cues.zh: 我承认这一点。

cues.en: Did I think it would work? I really wasn't sure. You know what? I was not trained as a psychotherapy, as an interventionist researcher.
cues.zh: 我觉得它会有效吗？我真不确定。你知道吗？我并没有接受过心理治疗师或干预研究者的训练。

cues.en: I was doing basic
cues.zh: 我当时在做基础

cues.en: neuroscience psychopathology.
cues.zh: 神经科学精神病理学。

cues.en: But I had a passion to see this epidemic brought to its knees. I had a passion to treat individuals whom I knew who had tried everything
cues.zh: 但我热切希望看到这场流行病被彻底击垮。我热切希望治疗那些我认识、已经试过一切办法的人

cues.en: and were still depressed. And so,
cues.zh: 却仍然抑郁。于是，

cues.en: with great trepidation, we set out to design this program.
cues.zh: 我们怀着极大的忐忑，开始设计这个项目。

cues.en: The results have exceeded my wildest dreams.
cues.zh: 结果超乎我最疯狂的想象。

cues.en: There
cues.zh: 总共

cues.en: are
cues.zh: 有

cues.en: six major elements. I'm going to run through them as quickly as I can in our remaining time. The first is exercise.
cues.zh: 六个主要要素。我会在剩余时间里尽可能快地讲一遍。第一个是运动。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: exercise is good for us. Many of can I see a show of hands? How many of you came in here today knowing
cues.zh: 锻炼对我们有好处。很多人——能举个手吗？你们有多少人今天来这儿时知道

cues.en: that exercise is really really good for us? Right? Every hand goes up. Now,
cues.zh: 锻炼对我们真的真的很有好处？对吧？所有人都举手了。那么，

cues.en: has it changed your behavior?
cues.zh: 它改变你的行为了吗？

cues.en: For some, yes.
cues.zh: 对一些人来说，是的。

cues.en: Everybody knows that exercise is good for us. Here's the problem.
cues.zh: 大家都知道锻炼对我们有好处。问题在这里。

cues.en: Many people have trouble making it happen. And you know what? A lot of people don't realize just how good. Exercise... I'm going say something that may be a little bit controversial. I'm going go ahead and say it. And I'm not speaking metaphorically. Exercise is medicine.
cues.zh: 很多人难以付诸行动。你知道吗？很多人并没意识到它到底有多好。锻炼……我要说点可能有点争议的话。我这就直说。我不是在打比方。锻炼就是药。

cues.en: Exercise literally is medicine. It changes the brain and the body in beneficial ways that are more powerful than any pill you can take.
cues.zh: 运动真的就是良药。它以有益的方式改变大脑和身体，效果比你能吃到的任何药片都更强。

cues.en: Yeah, I said it.
cues.zh: 没错，我就是这么说的。

cues.en: More powerful than any pill you can... In fact, I'm going to say something even more controversial.
cues.zh: 比你能吃到的任何药片都更强……事实上，我要说一个更有争议的观点。

cues.en: If you could take the neurological and physiological effects of exercise and capture them in a pill,
cues.zh: 如果你能把运动对神经和生理的影响提取出来，装进一颗药片里，

cues.en: all the beneficial effects on neural signaling in the brain, the anti aging effects all the way down to the level of chromosomes in every cell of your body,
cues.zh: 包括对大脑神经信号传导的所有有益影响，以及一直深入到身体每个细胞染色体层面的抗衰老效果，

cues.en: the mental clarity enhancing effects.
cues.zh: 还有提升头脑清晰度的效果。

cues.en: I believe... Tell me if you think I'm crazy. I believe
cues.zh: 我相信……如果你们觉得我疯了，就告诉我。我相信

cues.en: that pill would become the best selling drug of all time.
cues.zh: 那种药丸会成为史上最畅销的药物。

cues.en: And I I think people would pay any price to have it.
cues.zh: 而且我觉得，人们会不惜一切代价得到它。

cues.en: There's a problem though. We don't exercise.
cues.zh: 但有个问题。我们不锻炼。

cues.en: We don't.
cues.zh: 我们不锻炼。

cues.en: CDC again tells us that sixty percent of all American adults get no regular physical activity.
cues.zh: CDC再次告诉我们，60%的美国成年人没有规律运动。

cues.en: And yet, if we look at hunter gatherer groups,
cues.zh: 然而，如果我们看看狩猎采集群体，

cues.en: they get four or more hours of vigorous activity every day. In fact, they look like elite athletes,
cues.zh: 他们每天进行四小时以上的剧烈运动。事实上，他们看起来像精英运动员，

cues.en: even when they're in middle age and beyond.
cues.zh: 即使到了中年甚至更年长也是如此。

cues.en: Here's the thing I love though. If you ask them, they will tell you they do not exercise.
cues.zh: 不过我最喜欢的一点是：你问他们，他们会说自己不锻炼。

cues.en: They don't. They do not work out.
cues.zh: 他们不锻炼。他们真的不健身。

cues.en: Working out would be crazy to them. What do they do? They live.
cues.zh: 对他们来说，健身简直离谱。那他们做什么？他们生活。

cues.en: They live.
cues.zh: 他们就是生活。

cues.en: Here is...
cues.zh: 下面说……

cues.en: Yeah, I know. I know. I like it too.
cues.zh: 对，我知道。我知道。我也喜欢。

cues.en: Here's the dirty little secret
cues.zh: 这就是那个不光彩的小秘密

cues.en: in the business.
cues.zh: 行业里的。

cues.en: And I really want you, if you remember nothing else from this talk, exercise is not natural.
cues.zh: 我真的希望你们，如果这场演讲别的都没记住，就记住：锻炼并不自然。

cues.en: We are designed to be physically active in the service of adaptive goals. We are not designed to exercise.
cues.zh: 我们天生要为适应性目标而身体活动。我们并不是天生要锻炼。

cues.en: When you put a lab rat on a treadmill and crank that thing up to the point where it's moving faster than it wants to move, you know what it'll do if you let it? It'll squat down on its haunches and the treadmill starts to wear the fur and the skin right off its backside.
cues.zh: 当你把一只实验鼠放上跑步机，把速度调到超过它愿意跑的程度，你知道如果放开它会怎样吗？它会蹲坐下来，然后跑步机就开始把它屁股上的毛和皮都磨掉。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: it kinda feels our pain. Right? When
cues.zh: 它多多少少能体会到我们的痛苦。对吧？当你

cues.en: you stare at a piece of exercise equipment,
cues.zh: 盯着一件健身器材看时，

cues.en: there is a piece of your brain that's screaming out, don't do it.
cues.zh: 你脑子里有一部分在尖叫：别做。

cues.en: You're not going anywhere
cues.zh: 你靠那玩意儿

cues.en: on that thing.
cues.zh: 哪儿也去不了。

cues.en: So how do we solve this conundrum?
cues.zh: 那怎么解决这个难题呢？

cues.en: In our treatment program,
cues.zh: 在我们的治疗项目里，

cues.en: we've done two things. We've made exercise natural and we've made it social.
cues.zh: 我们做了两件事：让运动变得自然，也让它变得社交化。

cues.en: What's the most natural activity in the world? Walking.
cues.zh: 世上最自然的活动是什么？走路。

cues.en: And guess what? Brisk walking, you know the kind, like you're late for the bus, like you might miss your plane, that kind of walking,
cues.zh: 猜怎么着？快走，你知道那种走法，像赶公交快迟到了，像可能赶不上飞机，就是那种走法，

cues.en: will get your pulse up in the aerobic range and that's where it needs to be
cues.zh: 会让你的脉搏升到有氧区间，而这正是它该在的位置，

cues.en: based on your age. Depending on your age, it needs to be... Your pulse needs to be between about one twenty and one fifty.
cues.zh: 这取决于你的年龄。根据年龄不同，它应该是……你的脉搏大概要在 120 到 150 之间。

cues.en: That's enough
cues.zh: 这就够了

cues.en: to enhance signaling in your dopamine circuits, your serotonin circuits.
cues.zh: 来增强多巴胺回路和血清素回路的信号传导。

cues.en: It's been tested
cues.zh: 它已经过测试

cues.en: head to head against Zoloft twice.
cues.zh: 两次与 Zoloft 头对头比较。

cues.en: In the long term, it won.
cues.zh: 长期来看，它赢了。

cues.en: At what dose? Thirty minutes, three times a week. That's a low dose. It can change your life.
cues.zh: 什么剂量？每周三次，每次三十分钟。这是低剂量。它能改变你的人生。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: I wish I had time to cover everything else that we need to cover, but I'm going tell you about one more thing,
cues.zh: 我真希望能把其他要讲的都讲完，但还要再说一件事，

cues.en: omega three fats.
cues.zh: Omega-3 脂肪酸。

cues.en: Did you know that your brain is mostly made out of fat?
cues.zh: 你知道吗？你的大脑主要由脂肪构成。

cues.en: Did you know
cues.zh: 你知道吗？

cues.en: the brain is 60% fat by dry weight? So if somebody calls you a fat head,
cues.zh: 按干重算，大脑有 60% 是脂肪？所以要是有人叫你“肥脑袋”，

cues.en: they might be paying you a compliment.
cues.zh: 那可能是在夸你。

cues.en: Alright. Here's the thing.
cues.zh: 好，事情是这样的。

cues.en: Our bodies can make all the fats that we need with two exceptions. They're called essential fats. You've heard of them. Omega six's, Omega three's. They play complementary roles in the body and the brain.
cues.zh: 我们身体能合成所需的全部脂肪，只有两个例外。它们叫必需脂肪酸。你应该听说过：Omega-6 和 Omega-3。它们在身体和大脑中扮演互补的角色。

cues.en: Omega six's are inflammatory.
cues.zh: Omega-6 会引发炎症。

cues.en: Omega three's are anti inflammatory.
cues.zh: Omega-3 则抗炎。

cues.en: We need them in balance. We're designed to have them in balance.
cues.zh: 我们需要它们保持平衡。我们的身体天生就需要它们保持平衡。

cues.en: Omega three's come from grasses and plants and algae and the animals that eat them. Omega six's from grains and nuts and seeds and the animals that eat them, which is by the way most of our meat supply.
cues.zh: Omega-3 来自牧草、植物、藻类，以及吃这些东西的动物。Omega-6 来自谷物、坚果、种子，以及吃这些东西的动物——顺便说，我们的大部分肉类供应都是这样来的。

cues.en: Our hunter gatherer ancestors got omega sixes and omega threes in the optimal balance, is roughly one to one. We can do fine at two to one. We can probably even do okay at three to one. But guess what? The modern American diet, is riddled
cues.zh: 我们的狩猎采集祖先摄入的 Omega-6 和 Omega-3 处于最佳比例，大约是一比一。二比一我们也还行。三比一大概也还过得去。但你知道吗？现代美国饮食，充斥着

cues.en: with fast food,
cues.zh: 快餐，

cues.en: and processed food,
cues.zh: 和加工食品，

cues.en: and grain fed meat.
cues.zh: 以及谷饲肉类。

cues.en: You see the ratio there? 17
cues.zh: 你看到那个比例了吗？17

cues.en: to one.
cues.zh: 比一。

cues.en: 17 to one. Things are way out of balance. It's very heavily inflammatory, it's very heavily present.
cues.zh: 17比1。情况严重失衡。它非常促炎，含量也非常高。

cues.en: And that suggests to us, of course, that if we could supplement with omega threes, that might just be antidepressant.
cues.zh: 这当然提示我们，如果能补充 omega-3，那可能就有抗抑郁作用。

cues.en: Guess what? Over a dozen controlled research trials have now shown this to be the case.
cues.zh: 你猜怎么着？现在已有十多项对照研究试验表明情况确实如此。

cues.en: What's the antidepressant dose? I'm going leave you with this hopefully important tip.
cues.zh: 抗抑郁的剂量是多少？最后我要留给你们一个可能很重要的提示。

cues.en: The best research suggests that there's a specific Omega-three molecule that's called EPA.
cues.zh: 最好的研究表明，有一种特定的 Omega-3 分子叫作 EPA。

cues.en: And at a dose, this is a pretty high dose,
cues.zh: 而在某个剂量下，这是相当高的剂量，

cues.en: of one thousand to two thousand mg per day,
cues.zh: 也就是每天一千到两千毫克，

cues.en: it's shown to be antidepressant. Many of our patients have benefited
cues.zh: 它显示出抗抑郁作用。我们的许多患者获益

cues.en: remarkably,
cues.zh: 非常显著，

cues.en: not just with respect to their depression, but other inflammatory
cues.zh: 不仅是他们的抑郁，还有其他炎症

cues.en: conditions as well.
cues.zh: 状况也是如此。

cues.en: My my own story, when I began supplementing with Omega three's several years ago, the tendonitis in my knees went away, and I could start running full court basketball
cues.zh: 我自己的经历是，几年前我开始补充 Omega-3 时，膝盖的肌腱炎消失了，我又能开始打全场篮球

cues.en: again. The dryness in my eyes cleared up, and I could keep wearing my contacts.
cues.zh: 了。我眼睛的干涩也好了，我也能继续戴隐形眼镜。

cues.en: It's it's remarkably
cues.zh: 它、它真的非常

cues.en: health promoting
cues.zh: 有益健康

cues.en: in many different ways. Now,
cues.zh: 在很多方面都是。现在，

cues.en: for those of you who want to get more details about this treatment program, I'm just going to zip ahead
cues.zh: 想进一步了解这个治疗方案细节的人，我就赶紧往下讲了

cues.en: because I'm out of time.
cues.zh: 因为我没时间了。

cues.en: There's a lot more to share with you. I don't really talk about cows.
cues.zh: 还有很多要跟你们分享。我其实不怎么谈奶牛。

cues.en: We are designed as a very social species.
cues.zh: 我们天生是高度社会化的物种。

cues.en: We're designed to connect. Did you know that FaceTime,
cues.zh: 我们天生需要连接。你知道吗，FaceTime，

cues.en: time in the physical presence of our loved ones, actually puts the brakes on our stress response?
cues.zh: 与亲人实际相处的时间，其实会抑制我们的压力反应？

cues.en: Did you know that our ancestors
cues.zh: 你知道我们的祖先

cues.en: spent all day, every day in the company
cues.zh: 每天从早到晚都待在

cues.en: of their loved ones, their friends?
cues.zh: 所爱之人和朋友身边吗？

cues.en: Think about the extensive FaceTime they shared with the people that matter most.
cues.zh: 想想他们和最在乎的人共享了多少 FaceTime 时光。

cues.en: And what have we done? We've traded
cues.zh: 而我们做了什么？我们把

cues.en: FaceTime
cues.zh: FaceTime

cues.en: for screen time.
cues.zh: 换成了屏幕时间。

cues.en: FaceTime for Facebook. Is that better?
cues.zh: FaceTime 换成了 Facebook。这样更好吗？

cues.en: And the result is devastating.
cues.zh: 结果是灾难性的。

cues.en: The result is devastating. We are born to connect. We need that connection in our treatment protocol.
cues.zh: 结果是灾难性的。我们天生就要连接。在我们的治疗方案里，我们需要这种连接。

cues.en: We work very, very hard to help each depressed individual resist the urge to withdraw because when you are ill, your body tells you to shut down and pull away.
cues.zh: 我们非常非常努力地帮助每一位抑郁患者抵抗退缩的冲动，因为当你生病时，身体会告诉你要停下来、远离他人。

cues.en: When you are physically ill with the flu, that's adaptive. When you have clinical depression,
cues.zh: 当你身体患上流感时，这是适应性的。但当你患上临床抑郁症时，

cues.en: it's the worst thing in the world you can do, even though every fiber of your being is telling you exactly the opposite.
cues.zh: 这就是你能做的最糟糕的事，哪怕你全身的每一根神经都在告诉你完全相反的做法。

cues.en: We've got lots of good data on our outcomes, and as I've said, they've exceeded our wildest expectations.
cues.zh: 我们有很多关于疗效的良好数据，而且正如我所说，它们超出了我们最疯狂的预期。

cues.en: Most of the patients that have come to us have tried meds, and they haven't gotten
cues.zh: 来找我们的患者大多试过药物，但并没有

cues.en: well.
cues.zh: 好转。

cues.en: Most of them have tried traditional therapy, and it hasn't been the answer.
cues.zh: 他们大多数人试过传统治疗，但也没能解决问题。

cues.en: The majority have gotten well as they've been willing to change the way they live. We had a man
cues.zh: 大多数人愿意改变生活方式后就好转了。我们遇到过一位男士

cues.en: a year and a half ago who'd been fighting depression
cues.zh: 一年半前，他一直在与抑郁症抗争

cues.en: for forty one years
cues.zh: 长达四十一年

cues.en: consecutively.
cues.zh: 连续不断。

cues.en: And it was one of the happiest days of my life when he came into a session
cues.zh: 他来做咨询时，那是我一生中最开心的日子之一

cues.en: after fourteen weeks,
cues.zh: 十四周后，

cues.en: and he looked around the room with tears in his eyes and said,
cues.zh: 他眼里含着泪，环顾房间说：

cues.en: this is what I remembered it felt like to be free.
cues.zh: 这就是我记忆中自由的感觉。

cues.en: It can happen. Now, we're still working to improve this program, we're still working to make it better. I wish I had time to share with you some of the things we're learning.
cues.zh: 这是可能发生的。我们仍在努力改进这个项目，仍在努力让它变得更好。我真希望能有时间跟大家分享我们最近学到的一些东西。

cues.en: For those of you who want to learn more about it, I'd invite you to go to our website. We have lots of details.
cues.zh: 想了解更多细节的朋友，欢迎访问我们的网站，上面有大量详细内容。

cues.en: I wish you all
cues.zh: 祝大家

cues.en: a joyful and depression free life. Thank you.
cues.zh: 过上快乐、远离抑郁的生活。谢谢。
